channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

Nature Communications: Three-dimensional chromatin architecture is rapidly restored after DNA replication
item.description: Here, the authors show that factors involved in DNA looping bind DNA immediately after replisome passage and that loops are reformed within 10 min of DNA replication.

item.title: Nature Communications: GSNO-functionalized hydroxyapatite nanofertilizer for prolonged delivery, detoxification, and yield improvement in maize
item.description: Unstable nitric oxide donors limit agricultural uses. Here, the authors report on the immobilization of S-nitrosoglutathione onto humic acid-coated hydroxyapatite nanoparticles which reduces ROS levels, enhances antioxidant enzyme activity, and secondary metabolic synthesis while improving soil health.

item.title: Nature Communications: Learning stochasticity via a nonparametric approach to state-dependent noise estimation
item.description: Trine is a nonparametric kernel-based framework for inferring state-dependent noise from time-series data. Using a three-stage regression approach, it uncovers hidden stochastic dynamics without requiring predefined functional forms.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural and functional insights into a Zn 2+ -transporting P-type ATPase
item.description: Zinc is essential for cellular metal homeostasis, but the molecular mechanisms of zinc-transporters remain poorly understood. Here, the authors reveal the structure and regulatory mechanism of a zinc-transporting P-type ATPase, providing insights into zinc uptake and autoregulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Epithelial-mesenchymal Wnt crosstalk directs planar cell polarity in the developing cochlea
item.description: Patterning of cochlear hair cells is governed by planar cell polarity. Here, the authors show that multiple Wnt proteins from epithelial and mesenchymal compartments control cochlear elongation, hair cell patterning and core planar cell polarity proteins.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deep learning coupled with scalable domain-specific structural validation expands RNA virus discovery from metatranscriptomes
item.description: Here, the authors develop Rider, a method that integrates protein language modelling with domain-specific structural validation to detect divergent RNA viruses across more than 10,000 metatranscriptomes, including long polyproteins and short fragments.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolite correlation networks reveal complex phenotypes of adaptation-driving mutations
item.description: Adaptive mutations often reshape metabolism in complex ways, making it difficult to identify which changes improve fitness. This study shows that metabolite correlation networks reveal system-level metabolic reorganization and pinpoint metabolites linked to adaptive mechanisms.

item.title: Nature Communications: Laminar architecture of a decision circuit in the mouse orbitofrontal cortex
item.description: Economic choices rely on orbitofrontal cortex. The authors show that input and output variables are primarily encoded in superficial and deep layers, respectively, revealing a laminar organization in the decision circuit in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: The ongoing invasion of the endogenous retrovirus Kuruka in natural Drosophila melanogaster populations
item.description: Transposable elements are mobile DNA sequences that can copy themselves and spread between species. This study finds that Kuruka , a retrovirus-like transposon, invaded Drosophila melanogaster within the last decade and is still spreading worldwide.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reconstituting human and SV40 replisomes with Okazaki fragment maturation reveals synchronized leading- and lagging-strand synthesis
item.description: DNA replication must coordinate continuous copying of one strand with stepwise copying of the other as fragments that are processed and joined. Here, the authors rebuild human and SV40 replication systems and reveal how priming, enzyme recycling, and fragment maturation synchronize both strands.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hierarchical regulation of oxygen-sensing through coupled transducers in Arabidopsis thaliana
item.description: The PLANT CYSTEINE OXIDASE (PCO) N-degron pathway contributes to oxygen sensing in plants. Here the authors identify HYPOXIA TRANSDUCER1 (HYT1) as a substrate of PCO and show it forms a coherent feed-forward loop with ERFVII transcription factors to ensure a robust response to reduced oxygen.

item.title: Nature Communications: A modular synthetic promoter toolkit for programmable gene control in activated and chronically stimulated T cells
item.description: Achieving programmable gene regulation remains a challenge for engineering T cells. Here the authors characterize a library of synthetic promoters, responsive to seven endogenous T cell transcription factors, that show broad dynamic range of inducibility and basal expression.

item.title: Nature Communications: A hypothalamic circuit links high-fat diet exposure to anxiety-like behavior and anxiety-associated hyperphagia
item.description: Obesity and anxiety often co-occur, but their neural link is unclear. Here, authors show that an Arc-PVN-LHA hypothalamic circuit coordinates HFD-associated anxiety-like behavior and feeding in a state-dependent manner.

item.title: Nature Communications: MAP2-mediated integrin dysregulation reprograms cancer cell plasticity in hepatocellular carcinoma
item.description: Cancer cell plasticity contributes to drug resistance and metastasis in liver cancer. Here, authors show that targeting MAP2 with estramustine phosphate disrupts cancer stemness and enhances sensitivity to sorafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: WLG coordinates multi-stress tolerance in rice by regulating DST-dependent H 2 O 2 homeostasis and stomatal aperture
item.description: Abiotic stresses reduce rice growth. Here, the authors show that E3 ubiquitin ligase WLG enhances tolerance to drought, salt, and heat via a molecular mechanism that increases guard cell hydrogen peroxide accumulation and limits water loss.

item.title: Nature Communications: Stk1 is required for BlaR1-mediated broad-spectrum β-lactam resistance in epidemic-causing strains of Staphylococcus aureus
item.description: In this study, the authors demonstrate that targeting Stk1, which activates the resistance regulator BlaR1, could potentiate synthetic lethality to β-lactams in the majority of naturally isolated strains of MRSA, using a combination of biochemical and genetic methods.

item.title: Nature Communications: RNA binding proteome profiling reveals RNA-dependent activation of oncogenic host signaling during KSHV infection
item.description: Researchers mapped the RNA-binding proteins of a cancer-causing herpesvirus (KSHV) and found that the viral protein vIRF1 uses RNA to switch on a host growth-signaling pathway the virus needs to replicate in B cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic architecture of MRI-derived cervical spinal cord morphology reveals sensory-motor axis and systemic disease associations
item.description: A genome-wide association study of cervical spinal cord morphology using UK Biobank brain MRI data identifies 179 genetic loci shaping spinal cord morphology, revealing its links to systemic health.

item.title: Nature Communications: Topology-enhanced machine learning for speech signal processing
item.description: Topological data analysis had shown promise in capturing intrinsic structural features of complex data. Here, the authors integrate topological data analysis with machine learning to capture structural features in consonant classification while enhancing interpretability and robustness against noise compared to traditional techniques.

item.title: Nature Communications: Profilin promotes lamellipodium protrusion by tuning the antagonistic activities of capping protein and VASP
item.description: Genetic disruption combined with mathematical modeling establish the actin monomer binding protein profilin as promoter of Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin network formation and tuner of the antagonistic activities of the growing actin filament end regulators VASP and capping protein.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular mechanism of calcium inhibition in viral channelrhodopsins
item.description: Giant viruses encode light-gated channels that control calcium signals in infected cells. Here the authors reveal how calcium binds inside OLPVR1 and blocks the structural changes needed for ion flow.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cholesterol maintains the degradative capacity of lysosomes during clearance and recycling of dysfunctional mitochondria
item.description: Damaged mitochondria are cleared by lysosomes. Here, authors show that ER-to-lysosome cholesterol transport preserves lysosomal degradative function during mitophagy, enabling efficient recycling of lipids and their storage in lipid droplets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cenozoic losses of tree diversity constrain climatic adaptation of Western and Central European forests
item.description: This study shows that European tree diversity significantly declined over the Cenozoic due to colder conditions and glaciations. The loss of many heat-tolerant species constrains the resilience of European forests to the warming climate.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quantitative proteomics reveals coordinated changes in the proteome during replicative senescence
item.description: Senescence involves a massive reorganization of cellular components. This study shows that changes in ribosomal proteins and the ubiquitin-proteasome system are distinctive features of replicative senescence when compared to other cellular stresses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Automated screening of autism via a pretrained vision-language model in naturalistic caregiver-child interactions
item.description: Here, the authors develop Autism-CLIP, a vision–language model for automated early autism screening using 3-min home videos of toddlers aged 15–24 months.

item.title: Nature Communications: A scaffolding element rewires local 3D chromatin architecture during differentiation
item.description: Cell differentiation induces a 3D chromatin rewiring at the Zfp608 locus, driven by active transcription and a dual-function enhancer-scaffolding element that fosters key long-range interactions using both CTCF-dependent and independent mechanisms.

item.title: Nature Communications: Direct measurement of protein dipoles reveals the mechanism for like-charge adsorption on silica
item.description: Negatively charged particles are expected to adsorb with difficulty onto negatively charged surfaces but some proteins do. In this study, the authors use ferritin as a model protein particle to study its adsorption onto a negatively charged silica surface and explain the electrostatics of this like-charge attraction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Loss of NCOA6 protein causes aggressive prostate cancer with EGFR overexpression and dependency
item.description: EGFR is frequently overexpressed in prostate cancer. Here, the authors show that the transcriptional co-activator NCOA6 and the nuclear transcription factor NFY form a regulatory complex that restricts EGFR overexpression and suppresses prostate cancer development.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular dynamics guided all-atom reconstruction of cryo-ET maps reveals mechanisms of histone tail mediated chromatin compaction
item.description: This study combines molecular dynamics simulations with cryo-electron tomography to reconstruct native chromatin structures and reveal how histone tails interact with DNA and each other to promote chromatin compaction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural transition of the immature poxvirus scaffold from preassembly to the scaffold lattice
item.description: Scaffold protein governs the morphology of immature poxvirus particles. Here the authors report cryo-electron microscopy structures of in vitro assemblies and demonstrate a transition from a preassembly state to a fully assembled scaffold upon structural reorganization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plants recognize identity and intensity of herbivores to adaptively reconfigure metabolism
item.description: Using untargeted metabolomics and herbivore bioassays, the authors demonstrate that plants exhibit species-specific metabolic defense against multiple herbivore species. This process depends on both phytohormone and membrane receptor functioning.

item.title: Nature Communications: Integrated pangenomics and population genomics reveal climate adaptation and maladaptation in an East Asian tree
item.description: Understanding the genetic responses of trees to current and future climates is vital in the face of climate change. This study uses genomic datasets to reveal the genetic basis of climate adaptation and maladaptation in an East Asian tree species.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cryo-EM structure of human Na + /H + exchanger NHA1 in an inward-open conformation
item.description: Here the authors report the cryo-EM structure of human NHA1, a sodium-proton exchanger essential for sperm motility, revealing an inward-open conformation and an elevator-like transport mechanism. Mutagenesis and functional assays further identify key residues governing ion transport.

item.title: Nature Communications: WDR82 code coordinates transcription and pre-mRNA 3′-end processing through regulated phosphorylation
item.description: Phosphorylation links transcription to pre-mRNA maturation, but how remains unclear. Here, the authors show that the PP1 phosphatase, guided by PNUTS and WDR82, uses Symplekin to connect the 3′-end processing machinery to Pol II, coupling transcription termination with mRNA cleavage.

item.title: Nature Communications: On-demand design of controlled-release systems using an expert-mimic AI framework
item.description: Here the authors develop an AI framework called E-MAF that, starting from a desired release profile, couples process-aware prediction with expert-mimic evolutionary search to generate interpretable, lab-ready formulations for controlled release systems.

item.title: Nature Communications: Interrogating DNA methylation associated with Lewy body pathology in a cross brain-region and multi-cohort study
item.description: Lewy body pathology is associated with widespread molecular changes in the brain. Here, the authors identify DNA methylation alterations linked to increasing Lewy body burden, revealing disease-specific and shared epigenetic signatures across neurodegenerative disorders and implicating regulatory variation at the SNCA locus.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sero-catalytic and spatial modeling of dengue virus force of infection in Timor-Leste
item.description: Dengue is a public health concern in tropical and subtropical regions. Here, the authors present findings from a national, population-representative serological survey in Timor Leste and identify substantial spatial variation in force of infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: LENG8 granule regulates alternative polyadenylation in mammals
item.description: This work identifies LENG8 granules, a distinct membraneless organelle regulating alternative polyadenylation and engaging in crosstalk with nuclear speckles. These granules facilitate proximal poly(A) site selection in a YTHDC1-m⁶A-dependent manner.

item.title: Nature Communications: Compound Z247611722 Exhibits Antifungal Activity by Inhibiting Serine Palmitoyltransferase
item.description: This study identifies and characterizes Z247611722, a novel fungicidal compound active against multiple Candida species, and demonstrates that it inhibits sphingolipid biosynthesis by targeting serine palmitoyltransferase.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ablation of CDK6 and STAT5B rewires T cell developmental dynamics and prevents ALK + lymphoma formation
item.description: Although CDK6 and STAT5B are established oncogenic drivers, how they cooperate during lymphoma initiation remains poorly understood. The authors show that combined Cdk6 and Stat5b deletion completely prevents ALK-driven anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL) tumorigenesis, and suggest a prognostic signature linked to poor outcome in ALCL.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mobile genetic elements drive a plasmid fusion and deletion lifecycle shaping evolution and antimicrobial resistance
item.description: Plasmids drive bacterial adaptation, but how their diversity arises has remained unclear. Here, they show that in Staphylococcus aureus , mobile genetic elements repeatedly fuse and delete plasmids, reshaping gene content under competing pressures and accelerating the emergence and persistence of multidrug resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cryo-EM sample preparation with soft-landing and laser flash melting
item.description: Laser flash melting of a cryo-EM sample that is prepared by soft-landing mass spectrometry and subsequent deposition of amorphous ice restores some particles to near-native shape, pointing towards more reliable cryo-EM sample preparation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plasma autoantibody profiling via PhIP-seq and machine learning for diagnosis of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
item.description: Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma is often diagnosed in later stages, which limits potential treatment options. Here, the authors develop a PhIP-seq model to diagnose oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma across multiple cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effect of dietary chickpea structures on the small intestine metabolome and microbiome: a randomised crossover trial
item.description: Here, using spatially time-resolved mapping of the human gut, the authors characterize how food structure shapes metabolites, the microbiome and hormones linked to glucose and appetite, and suggest that oral bacteria influence the ileal microbiome.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chromatin modifiers KMT2D, cBAF, and p300 cooperatively facilitate de novo binding of transcription factors on enhancers
item.description: Here, the authors show that chromatin modifiers are required for transcription factors to bind new enhancers, revealing that enhancer landscapes are built through cooperation rather than a strict step-by-step order.

item.title: Nature Communications: Iterative and data-driven ortholog mining enables reliable discovery of stereoselective ketoreductases
item.description: Ketoreductases (KREDs) enable the stereoselective synthesis of chiral alcohols and are used in many industrial manufacturing routes, however, the identification of process-compatible enzymes with high activity and selectivity toward non-native substrates remains challenging. Here, the authors present an iterative ortholog mining strategy to efficiently explore and expand functional enzyme space of KREDs.

item.title: Nature Communications: Biofilm formation and dynamics in the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus
item.description: In this study, the authors show that Prochlorococcus picocyanobacteria form biofilms and dynamically transition between free-living and attached states with significantly different physiology, thus suggesting a role for these bacteria in deep-ocean carbon export.

item.title: Nature Communications: Assistive algorithms influence neural representations in motor brain-computer interfaces
item.description: Assistive algorithms are widely used in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but their effects on neural representations remain unclear. Here, the authors show that adaptive BCIs lead the brain to learn compact representations, suggesting assistive algorithms shape long-term credit assignment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tunneling nanotubes regulate mitochondrial homeostasis between glioblastoma and astrocytes, and between tumor cells in vivo
item.description: Tunneling nanotube-like (TNT) connections allow mitochondrial exchange between tumor cells and its tumor microenvironment. Here, the authors show that TNT connections mediate bidirectional mitochondrial transfer between glioblastoma tumor cells and astrocytes in vitro, and between head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cells in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multimodal data-driven clustering analysis of heart failure patients identifies two distinct patterns of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: Results from the PACIFIC-PRESERVED study
item.description: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is clinically heterogeneous, complicating efforts to identify patients at highest risk. Here, the authors show that integrating proteomics with machine learning reveals two biologically distinct subtypes with different prognoses, including a high-risk inflammatory cardiorenal phenotype.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effectiveness of the oral rotavirus vaccine ROTASIIL among children hospitalized with acute gastroenteritis in India
item.description: Here, using pooled data from two multi-center observational studies, the authors analyze the effectiveness of the ROTASIIL ® vaccine in protecting young children against moderate to severe rotavirus diarrhea, finding that three doses of this vaccine provided good protection, especially among younger children, highlighting the need for timely and complete vaccination.

item.title: Nature Communications: Privacy-preserving pangenome graphs
item.description: Here the authors present PanMixer, a framework that obfuscates haplotype paths in pangenome graphs to reduce privacy risk while preserving downstream utility.

item.title: Nature Communications: scTransMIL bridges patient-level disease states and single-cell transcriptomics for cancer screening and heterogeneity inference
item.description: Reliably linking patient-level cancer phenotypes to single-cell transcriptomes re-mains challenging due to limited cell-level labels. Here, the authors develop scTransMIL, a transformer-based multi-instance learning framework that identifies cancer states, cancer subtypes, and potential cancer biomarkers with good performance across datasets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hos2-mediated KatG1 decrotonylation orchestrates ROS scavenging in rice blast infection
item.description: Plants trigger reactive oxygen species (ROS) bursts to defend against pathogens. Here the authors report that decrotonylation and relocalization of the rice blast fungus KatG1 protein can activate fungal ROS responses and propose targeting of this pathway in fungicide development.

item.title: Nature Communications: Antagonistic roles of histone H3 lysine methyltransferases dictate tumor immune surveillance
item.description: Histone H3K36 methyltransferases are frequently altered in cancer, yet the distinct roles of H3K36 methylation states in tumorigenesis and immunity remain unclear. This study identifies an H3K36-dependent epigenetic circuit that controls endogenous retroviral elements (ERVs) repression and immune surveillance in KRAS-driven lung cancer models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Telomere length of both parents contributes to heritable POT1 cancer-predisposition syndrome
item.description: Using haplotype-specific nanopore sequencing, the authors show that cancer-associated POT1 mutations reshape telomere inheritance across generations through germline and post-fertilization remodeling of the shortest telomeres.

item.title: Nature Communications: GLM-Prior: a genomic language model for transferable sequence-derived priors in gene regulatory network inference
item.description: Gene regulatory network inference depends on high-quality prior knowledge, yet curated priors are often incomplete or unavailable across species and cell types. Here, authors present GLM-Prior, a genomic language model to predict transcription factor-target gene interactions from nucleotide sequence.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural and mechanistic insights into OCTN1-mediated transport and cancer cell proliferation
item.description: Here, the authors present cryo-EM structures of OCTN1, revealing its substrate binding and sodium-dependent rearrangements, and identify mebendazole as an OCTN1 inhibitor that suppresses cancer cell proliferation.

item.title: Nature Communications: RICTOR regulates an interspecies crosstalk that influences longevity through a methionine cycle-mitophagy axis
item.description: Physiological traits are modulated in response to diet. Here the authors show that RICTOR restrains host responses to vitamin B12 in C. elegans by modulating organellar quality control and regulating lifespan.

item.title: Nature Communications: BRAINCELL modelling platform for stochastic nanoscale organisation and dynamic extracellular signalling among neurons and glia
item.description: Fundamental properties of signal integration in brain circuits are not fully understood. To address several limitations of current biophysical models, the authors introduce a simulation platform, enabling realistic simulations of dynamic extracellular signaling in the brain, such as glia-neuron communications, axon-myelin interactions, and so on.

item.title: Nature Communications: Next-generation functional diagnostic paradigm for musculoskeletal diseases based on live SWIR imaging
item.description: Here, the authors develop a live SWIR imaging strategy to enable dynamic, multi-component functional diagnosis of musculoskeletal diseases. It visualizes synovial fluid flow during locomotion, reveals patellar maltracking, and shows bone and vascular kinematics during healing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deciphering the mechanisms of macrophage polarization through comprehensive analysis of cellular and cell-surface protein glycosylation
item.description: Macrophage polarization has profound implications in diseases and involves extensive remodeling of surface glycoproteins. Here, the authors map surface glycoproteins in macrophages with M1 or M2 phenotype and primary human macrophages, revealing phenotype-specific changes of surface glycoproteins.

item.title: Nature Communications: Angiotensin II exacerbates intracerebral hemorrhage in mice via heparin-like antithrombin activation and coagulation dysfunction
item.description: Here, the authors show that angiotensin II acts as a key coagulation regulator with heparin-like antithrombin activation function in mediating hemorrhage. Targeting the angiotensin II coagulation pathway could be a novel strategy to mitigate cerebral bleeding events.

item.title: Nature Communications: Learning reorganizes dendritic and stabilizes axon initial segment inhibitory synapses in CA1 pyramidal neurons
item.description: Using repeated brain imaging, the authors find that inhibitory synapses change at different rates across neuronal subcellular compartments in mouse CA1. Fear learning reorganizes dendritic connections but stabilizes those at the axon initial segment, which may aid memory recall.

item.title: Nature Communications: Preclinical and clinical investigation of VES001, an oral small molecule sortilin receptor inhibitor for the treatment of frontotemporal dementia: a first-in-human randomized placebo-controlled phase 1 trial
item.description: Treatment for frontotemporal dementia due to GRN haploinsufficiency (FTD-GRN) are lacking. Here, in this preclinical and Phase 1 clinical trial, the authors show that VES001, an oral small molecule sortilin inhibitor, is safe and well tolerated, and increased progranulin levels.

item.title: Nature Communications: Early coconut oil exposure suppresses chronic experimental Crohn’s disease via myristic acid and enhanced regulatory T cells
item.description: Here, the authors show that coconut oil and the fatty acid myristic acid suppress Crohn disease-like intestinal inflammation in mice through multiple mechanisms, supporting a potential role for these dietary fats in promoting protective immune gut responses in Crohn’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: CpG hypermethylation and WNT/AP-1 cooperativity define the epigenetic landscape and a clinical subgroup of high-risk pediatric adrenocortical carcinoma
item.description: Pediatric adrenocortical tumours (pACTs) are rare and difficult to treat. Here, the authors perform integrated multi-omics analysis of 214 pACTs and identify four distinct risk groups and potential therapeutic targets.

item.title: Nature Communications: CG14075/Mmt promotes amino acid catabolism and cooperates with AKH during starvation in Drosophila
item.description: How animals survive without food depends on more than stored fat and sugar. This study shows that the fruit fly hormone CG14075/Marmite helps redirect amino acid use during starvation, working with a key hormone, AKH, to sustain energy balance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reprogramming the Rossmann fold signature motif creates orthogonal redox biocatalysts
item.description: Developing NMN⁺ as an orthogonal redox cofactor could help biomanufacturing approach theoretical maximum yields. Here, the authors show that engineering the Rossmann fold can convert NAD(P)-dependent enzymes to selectively use the noncanonical cofactor NMN(H).

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiple Argonaute complexes orchestrate epigenetic silencing in the Arabidopsis germline
item.description: Long et al . reveal how reproductive small RNAs engage multiple Argonaute proteins to coordinate DNA methylation and post-transcriptional gene silencing in the Arabidopsis germline, supporting meiosis and fertility.

item.title: Nature Communications: Functional alignment of protein language models via reinforcement learning
item.description: Protein language models are powerful tools for generative protein design, but because they are trained solely on natural sequences, they often struggle to generate proteins with enhanced or non-natural functions. This work a general framework that aligns generative protein language models with experimentally defined functional objectives.

item.title: Nature Communications: Widespread declines of formerly common species reshape local assemblages over time
item.description: Human-driven environmental change is reshaping ecological communities worldwide. Analysing 4,748 sites across 129 studies, we show that formerly common species decline disproportionately compared to rare species in marine and terrestrial assemblages.

item.title: Nature Communications: A single-nucleus atlas of ligular region uncovers brassinosteroid-driven cell fate transitions controlling leaf angle in maize
item.description: Here the authors integrate single-nucleus transcriptomic and cellular analyse to reveal that brassinosteroid drives cell division, elongation, and subsequent lignification in the ligular region, thereby controlling leaf angle diversity in maize.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tumor-targeted IL-10 synergizes with IL-2 to enhance antitumor immunity while minimizing immune-related adverse events
item.description: IL2-based immunotherapies enhance anti-tumor immune responses, however, there is a significant risk of severe immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Here the authors show that combining a tumor-targeting cetuximab-based bispecific IL10 fusion protein with tumor-targeted IL2 enhances antitumor immunity and controls tumor growth while reducing IL2-associated irAEs through distinct IL-10R functions in dendritic cells and macrophages.

item.title: Nature Communications: The 11-hydroxy-jasmonic acid pathway expands jasmonate catabolic repertoire for stress-specific hormone attenuation in Arabidopsis
item.description: The plant hormone jasmonate undergoes complex enzymatic turnover that shape hormonal dynamics for optimal signaling. Here the authors show that separate enzyme systems catalyze stress induced formation of 11-OH- and 12-OH-jasmonic acid.

item.title: Nature Communications: Polyploid frequency decreases with elevation but increases with distance to glacial refugia in the Eastern European Alps
item.description: This study reveals that polyploid frequency of angiosperms decreases with elevation and increases with distance from glacial refugia in the Eastern European Alps, highlighting the role of historical range dynamics in shaping polyploid distributions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Leveraging high-throughput proteomics and AI-based protein folding to accelerate VAV1 molecular glue discovery
item.description: VAV1 is a blood-cell signaling protein linked to leukemia and autoimmune disease. Here, the authors discover CRBN molecular glues that degrade VAV1 via a non-canonical degron, using proteomics and AI-based structural modeling to guide the design of more potent degraders.

item.title: Nature Communications: TET2 loss triggers ssDNA gap accumulation and heightened PARP inhibitor sensitivity
item.description: Somatic mutations in DNMT3A and TET2 are common in age-related clonal haematopoiesis and hematopoietic neoplasms. Here, the authors show that loss of TET2, unlike DNMT3A, makes cells more sensitive to PARP inhibitors by disrupting DNA replication, suggesting TET2 mutations may help predict treatment response.

item.title: Nature Communications: Loss of oxytocin receptor function disrupts neural signatures of pair bonding and fidelity in the nucleus accumbens
item.description: Oxytocin receptor signaling in the nucleus accumbens supports pair bonding, but its role in attachment-related neural activity is unclear. Here, the authors show that Oxtr loss sex-specifically alters pair bonding and nucleus accumbens activity in prairie voles; in males, early activity predicts partner preference.

item.title: Nature Communications: Huntington’s disease vasculopathy is barrier-type-selective and arteriolar-dominant with spatially-coupled astrogliosis and reversible by S1pr1 stimulation
item.description: Here the authors map Huntington’s pathology by barrier and vessel type with two-photon imaging, mass-spec signatures and mouse/human data. They reveal arteriolar susceptibility, spatially matched astrocyte activation and S1pr1 stimulation as potential therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: PKM2 AP: a micropeptide inhibits vascular calcification via molecular glue-mediated ubiquitination of PKM2
item.description: The study identifies a micropeptide that protects against vascular calcification, a major complication of chronic kidney disease. The micropeptide acts through a molecular glue-like mechanism to promote PKM2 degradation, suppress glycolysis and reduce vascular calcification in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global brain activity links subcortical degeneration to cortical tau progressively across Braak regions over early Alzheimer’s disease stages
item.description: This study finds that reduced infra-slow global brain activity may link degeneration of a key subcortical cholinergic region to progressive cortical tau accumulation in early Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: SLC4A7/NBCn1 maintains intracellular pH to support mTORC1 activity and antibody-secreting cell differentiation
item.description: Environmental cues, such as pH, determine cellular differentiation and function, including that of immune cells. Here the authors identify SLC4A7, a Na + /HCO3–cotransporter as a critical and specific regulator of plasmablast differentiation genetic deletion of which in mice impairing antibody responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Discovery of an antagonist nanobody targeting the oxytocin receptor with tocolytic effect in mice
item.description: Preterm birth poses severe risks to mothers and newborns. Here, the authors identify an oxytocin receptor antagonist nanobody with tocolytic effects in mice, offering a potential roadmap for developing next generation tocolytic drugs.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of IgLON5 autoantibody recognition in autoimmune encephalitis
item.description: Anti-IgLON5 disease is a rare neuro-immunological disorder characterized by the production of autoantibodies against the cell adhesion molecule, IgLON5. Here, the authors examine the B cell receptor repertoire of an individual with this condition and present a cryo–electron microscopy structure of a patient-derived antibody clone in complex with IgLON5.

item.title: Nature Communications: RAISE quantifies RNA binding protein activity via transcriptomic profiling
item.description: Alternative splicing is regulated by RNA-binding proteins, but measuring their regulatory activity remains challenging. Here, the authors develop RAISE, a computational framework that integrates multimodal data to construct splicing regulatory networks and quantify activity from transcriptomic data.

item.title: Nature Communications: LGR5-positive fibroblasts orchestrate skin mechanoadaptation through JAK1 modulation
item.description: Mechanical stress induces LGR5+ fibroblasts that promote adaptive tissue remodeling by limiting fibrosis through JAK1 modulation. The study reveals a conserved mechanism of adaptation to mechanical stress and suggests a strategy for regenerative therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: 3D minichannel-morphed adipose stem cell-cartilage granule reconstituted tough grafts for repairing segmental tracheal defects in preclinical models
item.description: There, the authors develop a tracheal reconstruction strategy using 3D-printed minichannels with stem cell–cartilage composites in preclinical models. Bypassing cell expansion, these tough grafts achieve rapid vascularization and repair segmental airway defects.

item.title: Nature Communications: A neural circuit of food sight-promoted feeding and contextual memory in mice
item.description: Feeding can be regulated by sensory cues. This study identifies a multi-layer circuit that mediates food sight-promoted feeding and food-related memory in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: CReP-mediated control of eIF2α phosphorylation is a critical node in MYC-driven medulloblastoma
item.description: Group 3 (G3) medulloblastoma is an aggressive paediatric brain tumour with limited treatment options. Here, the authors show that CReP phosphatase maintains eIF2α activity, thereby protecting G3 MB cells from apoptosis, and that these cells are sensitive to eIF2α inactivation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Co-optimized volumetric muscle design for large dynamic deformations in versatile biohybrid robots
item.description: The authors combine computer simulation and experimental fabrication to co-design living muscle and its scaffold, optimizing the range of motion of bioactuators to power biohybrid robots that can jump, swim, walk and grip.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vivo CRISPR screens identify dual functions of DNMT3A in mediating tumor immune evasion
item.description: DNMT3A regulates the anti-tumor activity of CAR-T cells. Here, based on in vivo CRISPR screens, the authors identify tumor cell-intrinsic DNMT3A as a mediator of immune evasion, showing that DNMT3A modulates TNF signalling and cholesterol biosynthesis to impair CD8 T cell anti-tumor immunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cardiac fibroblast deletion of PTBP1 modulates the profibrotic response by alternative splicing
item.description: Post-transcriptional regulation of cardiac fibroblast phenotypes during fibrotic cardiac remodeling remains poorly defined. Here, the authors demonstrate that RNA-binding protein PTBP1 regulates alternative splicing to direct the profibrotic response in multiple cardiac injury models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chromosome-scale genomes and population resequencing resolve subgenome diversity and halophyte adaptation in Salicornia
item.description: Salicornia is a halophytic flowering plants in the family Amaranthaceae. Here, the authors report chromosome-scale genome assemblies for six Salicornia species and reveal subgenome diversity, species boundaries and signatures of halophyte adaptation.

item.title: Nature Communications: A cryptic symmetry switch allosterically controls how the PF4 self-protein turns into a pathogenic antigen
item.description: Platelet Factor 4 (PF4) is a chemokine involved in several physiological processes. Ma et al. discovered that an allosteric switch exposes cryptic PF4 epitopes, suggesting that stabilizing non-immunogenic conformations of self-proteins may suppress autoimmune responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Proteasome inhibition alleviates proteinuria in Lmx1b knock-in mice with dysfunctional LIM domains
item.description: Mutations in the LIM domains of LMX1B cause ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation and result in podocyte injury. Inhibition of the proteasome ameliorated renal symptoms in Lmx1b knock-in mice, thus providing proof of principle for a novel therapeutic strategy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic loneliness and isolation phenotypes and physical and mental health in older adults
item.description: Chronic loneliness was associated with poorer physical and mental health, while loneliness onset showed similar but weaker associations. Social isolation primarily affected mental health, while remission may confer cognitive benefits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Urban exposures, frailty, and mental illness in World Trade Center Health Program responders
item.description: Higher exposure to long-term air pollution, heat, and less neighborhood greenery is linked to increase in frailty and mental illness test scores among the World Trade Center (WTC) responders. These effects were stronger among those with higher WTC-related exposure histories.

item.title: Nature Communications: The kinase SPE-55 promotes localized assembly of the major sperm protein in Caenorhabditis elegans spermatocytes
item.description: In developing spermatocytes, proteins required for nematode sperm motility assemble into large complexes on the cytosolic side of Golgi-derived organelles. Here, the kinase SPE-55 is identified as a key nucleator of this localized assembly process.

item.title: Nature Communications: Himito: a graph-based toolkit for mitochondrial genome analysis using long reads
item.description: Himito is a graph-based toolkit for long-read mitochondrial genome analysis. It integrates NUMT filtering, haplotype assembly, variant calling, and methylation profiling, providing a comprehensive framework for studying mtDNA in aging and human disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Human testis-specific TTRP regulates circadian clock as an evolutionarily young natural antisense transcript of PER2
item.description: TTRP is an evolutionarily novel gene in higher Hominoidea that has been recruited to regulate the human circadian clock. As an antisense gene to PER2 , TTRP modulates circadian rhythms through both transcriptional interference and its encoded protein.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rapid changes in risk attitudes originate from Bayesian inference on parietal magnitude representations
item.description: Risk attitudes can shift across contexts and even between identical choices. Here, the authors show that as parietal payoff representations grow noisier, the brain leans more on prior beliefs, biasing perceived value and risk-taking.

item.title: Nature Communications: The hijacking of a wheat Exo70 -like protein by a fungal pathogen triggers disease
item.description: Tan spot is an economically important disease of wheat. Here the authors show that a deletion in the wheat gene Tsc2 , which encodes an Exo70-like protein, enables a fungal effector to hijack host immunity causing cell death and demonstrate practical routes to tan spot resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: ATAD-3 couples plasma membrane injury to mitochondrial Ca 2+ signaling
item.description: In this study, Xu et al. identify ATAD-3 as a context-dependent regulator of mitochondrial Ca²⁺ uptake that is activated by cellular injury through oligomerization and mitochondrial enrichment, independent of MCU-1.

item.title: Nature Communications: Directionality of transcriptional regulatory elements
item.description: Features of nascent RNA profiles such as transcriptional directionality at active promoters and enhancers encode rich information. Here, authors show that unidirectional elements differ from divergent ones in architecture, evolution, and function, revealing contributors of transcriptional directionality.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bacterial inoculation elicits changes to the coral epigenome
item.description: Pocillopora verrucosa corals were inoculated with a bacterial pathogen and/or a coral probiotic, then subjected to heat stress. Pathogen inoculation induced epigenetic and gene expression changes that were mitigated by probiotic co-inoculation.

item.title: Nature Communications: High-accuracy glycan de novo prediction for N- and O-linked glycopeptides across multiple fragmentation techniques
item.description: Protein glycosylation is difficult to analyse across glycan classes and fragmentation methods. Here, the authors present DeepGlycan, a model that predicts N- and Oglycan compositions from tandem mass spectra and supports analyses across tissues and disease datasets.

item.title: Nature Communications: BRWD1 directs B cell epigenetic states required for germinal center initiation, maintenance and function
item.description: The epigenetic reader BRWD1 is central for B cell progenitor development in the bone marrow, but its role in the adaptive immune response is not well understood. Here, the authors analyze conditional Brwd1 knockout and immunization models, finding transcriptional germinal center B cell subset identities to depend on BRWD1.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mapping high resolution, multidimensional phase diagrams of near-physiological protein condensates
item.description: Agarwal and colleagues present ExVivo PhaseScan, a scalable microfluidic approach for mapping high-resolution phase diagrams of complex multi-component condensates under near-physiological conditions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating the consequences of childhood adiposity on the human plasma proteome at four timepoints across the lifecourse
item.description: Childhood obesity can influence health across the lifespan, but its molecular effects at different ages are not fully understood. Here, the authors use lifecourse genetics to show that childhood adiposity alters circulating proteins from childhood into adulthood, identifying potential links to childhood asthma and breast cancer risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vascular and lymphatic dysregulation via non-EndoMT Col2a1 signaling in bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw
item.description: Bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (BRONJ) is a severe complication of antiresorptive therapy with poorly understood vascular mechanisms. Here, the authors identify vascular and lymphatic drivers of BRONJ and show that genetic ablation or silencing of Col2a1 restores endothelial homeostasis and rescues osteonecrotic lesions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Decoding the genomic repertoire of fosfomycin resistance genes in staphylococci
item.description: Here, the authors use 17,000 public genomes to systematically classify and unify nomenclature for fosfomycin resistance genes in Staphylococcus .

item.title: Nature Communications: Fecal microbiota transplantation for the decolonization of mucosal adherent-invasive Escherichia coli in Crohn’s disease: an open-label pilot study
item.description: Here, in a pilot study in humans, the authors provide proof of concept that fecal microbiota transplantation can be used for clearing harmful E. coli from the gut lining of people with Crohn’s disease, highlighting the potential of microbiome-targeted therapies in inflammatory bowel disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Assessing the use of automatic speech recognition and large language models for individuals with language impairments
item.description: Speech-enabled AI systems may be less reliable for people with language impairments. Here, the authors evaluate ASR-LLM pipelines across aphasia, child language impairment and dementia datasets, identifying transcript errors, repetition, and length as key factors affecting performance.

item.title: Nature Communications: A nested case-control study of air pollution and congenital heart defects via circulating proteins
item.description: Prenatal exposure to air pollution has been linked to risk of congenital heart defects (CHD). Here the authors report that periconception exposure, especially to NO₂, is associated with higher CHD risk and distinct maternal and cord blood protein signatures.

item.title: Nature Communications: Atlas of genetic architecture and exploratory temporal interaction networks of plasma protein-based organ and system aging
item.description: This study provides a comprehensive atlas integrating genetic, environmental, and interactive insights into organ and system aging using multiple plasma protein-based networks, informing future research on targeted anti-aging strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: A dual-site oral nanovaccine programs anti-colorectal tumor immunity from small intestinal priming to large intestinal boosting
item.description: Here the authors report the design and characterization of a nano-vaccine composed of antigen- and CpG-loaded nanoparticles stabilized by β glucan and plant-derived lipids, showing that, after oral administration, it induces immune priming in the small intestine as well as acts as in situ vaccine to trigger anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Explainable data generation from observed small samples by matrix tri-factorization
item.description: Here the authors propose an explainable data generation approach called EDG that operates under extreme sample scarcity by exploiting inherent low-dimensional principles contained in the observed high-dimensional data via matrix tri-factorization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Recurrent mechanisms of biallelic epigenetic inactivation reveal new putative tumour suppressor genes in prostate cancer
item.description: Epigenetic biallelic inactivation in prostate cancer remains to be explored. Here, the authors develop a computational method Epi2Hit that integrates the hemizygous genomic disruptions with patterns of hypermethylation at regulatory CpG sites to identify biallelic inactivation in tumour suppressor genes.

item.title: Nature Communications: A core transcriptional regulatory circuitry controls super-enhancer-driven activation of LGR5 in colorectal cancer
item.description: MYC can be transcriptionally regulated by distal super-enhancers (SEs) in cancers. Here, the authors show that MYC, along with ETS2 and FOXP1, form a core regulatory circuit that controls SE-driven transcription in colorectal cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deep learning CT signature for predicting early liver metastases in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
item.description: Predicting the risk of early liver micrometastases (ELM) is crucial for identifying patients who are most likely to benefit from neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) yet most deep learning models focus mainly on primary tumours. Here, the authors show that the non-invasive Mamba based model is able to integrate multi-phase spatiotemporal CT imaging features from both the primary pancreatic tumour and liver regions to predict the risk of ELM in PDAC.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD73 disruption with tumor-specific CRISPR/Cas9 nanoparticles reduces adenosine-mediated immunosuppression and amplifies response to chemotherapy
item.description: Extracellular adenosine, generated by the hydrolysis of ATP by CD39 and CD73, contributes to immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment (TME). Here the authors report that disruption of CD73 with tumor specific CRISPR/Cas9 nanoparticles reduces adenosine mediated immunosuppression in the TME and amplify response to chemo-immunotherapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Precision inflammation targeting via myeloperoxidase mediated antioxidant melanin nanomedicines for chronic inflammation therapy
item.description: Chronic inflammation threats health due to unspecific drugs. Here the authors show in hepatopulmonary syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease models, an anti-inflammatory melanin nanomedicine platform that targets inflamed tissues and is mediated by myeloperoxidase.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gut microbiota composition outperforms chronological age in predicting systemic inflammation and incident disease risk
item.description: Here, characterizing 1,199 adults, the authors find that gut bacteria patterns predict inflammation and future disease risk better than age, with an identified microbiota type showing signs of “inflammaging” decades earlier, while a diverse microbiota is linked to better health.

item.title: Nature Communications: Refining biopsy strategies stratified by PI-RADS score in men: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
item.description: Optimal biopsy strategies for lesions with Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) scores of 3-5 remain uncertain. Here, the authors show that for PI-RADS 3–5 lesions, saturation targeted biopsy and ipsilateral systematic biopsy combined with targeted biopsy (ips-SB + TB) exhibit comparable detection rates of clinically significant prostate cancer to systematic plus targeted biopsy (SB + TB), supporting refined biopsy strategies that challenge the necessity of bilateral systematic biopsy. However, targeted biopsy alone remains insufficient, and omitting systematic biopsy in PI-RADS 5 lesions is not supported by current evidence.

item.title: Nature Communications: Embryo selection by non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy in women of advanced maternal age: a randomized, clinical trial
item.description: Non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (niPGT-A) can detect embryo chromosomal aneuploidy by analyzing the cell-free DNA in embryo culture media, but evidence for clinical efficacy is insufficient. Here the authors report a randomised controlled trial involving 1,152 women aged 35–42 years that shows no difference in the primary outcome of ongoing pregnancy rate between the intervention group with niPGT-A and the control group with morphological selection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Arginine metabolism as a mutualistic strategy in the interaction between Porphyromonas gingivalis and Filifactor alocis
item.description: Complex microbial communities are often shaped by cooperation. Here, the authors show that high arginine levels suppress the periodontal pathogen Porphyromonas gingivalis, while Filifactor alocis helps it persist by breaking down arginine, revealing a metabolic partnership.

item.title: Nature Communications: A cytoskeleton-associated Plasmodium protein critical for organelle segregation
item.description: The Plasmodium cytoskeleton is critical for parasite replication. Here, Navarro et al identify and characterise a cytoskeleton-associated protein required for organelle segregation and asexual replication.

item.title: Nature Communications: CNIH4 regulates systemic metabolism and exercise adaptations in male mice primarily through the modulation of β-adrenergic receptor trafficking
item.description: Liu et al. show in male mice that CNIH4 helps adrenaline receptors reach cell surfaces, supporting skeletal muscle glucose use and uphill exercise performance, while promoting brown fat breakdown and heat production in adipose tissue.

item.title: Nature Communications: Puberty, pregnancy, and menopause show shared and distinct structural changes across the lifespan
item.description: Brain volumes decline during puberty and pregnancy, with both shared and distinct regional patterns, while menopause appears to briefly pause rather than speed up ongoing volume loss, as shown by this neuroimaging study directly comparing these three transitions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Canakinumab with chemoradiation and durvalumab consolidation in unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer: the phase I/II CHORUS trial
item.description: IL-1β targeting may attenuate myeloid-suppressive pathways and support antitumor immunity. Here, the authors report a phase I/II trial of concurrent canakinumab, an anti-IL-1β antibody, with chemoradiotherapy, followed by consolidation canakinumab plus the anti-PD-L1 antibody durvalumab, in patients with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tislelizumab plus lenvatinib in advanced fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma: a single-arm, phase 2 trial with metabolic biomarker analysis
item.description: Effective first-line treatments for fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma remain poorly defined, despite promising activity of immune checkpoint inhibitor– based combinations. There these authors report efficacy outcomes of a phase 2 clinical trial on tislelizumab plus lenvatinib in fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma patients.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multitask framework for automated multi-frame right upper quadrant ultrasound interpretation and clinical decision support
item.description: Authors developed an AI system for interpreting multi-frame right upper quadrant ultrasound examinations. Across three institutions, it classified findings, generated reports, and predicted the need for cholecystectomy.

item.title: Nature Communications: CBX4 stabilizes NEUROD1 through SUMO-ubiquitin crosstalk to delay β-cell senescence
item.description: As pancreatic β-cells age, CBX4 levels fall. Restoring CBX4 stabilizes the transcription factor NEUROD1 via SUMOylation and phase separation, counteracting its degradation to rejuvenate β-cell function and offering a new diabetes treatment avenue.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dysregulated tissue immunity in human fatal asthma
item.description: Immune mechanisms driving severe asthma and fatal outcomes remain elusive. Through cross-tissue immune profiling of organ donors who died of fatal asthma versus other causes, the authors here reveal mucosal immune dysregulation marked by enhanced T- and B-cell memory, reduced Tregs, and increased lung Th2 and Th1 effectors linked to priming in gut-associated lymph nodes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neoadjuvant PD1 plus CTLA-4 immune checkpoint blockade in surgically resectable recurrent glioblastoma: a randomized surgical window-of-opportunity trial
item.description: Here the authors report clinical and immunological outcomes of a randomized surgical window-of-opportunity trial designed to test whether dual immune checkpoint blockade targeting PD-1 and CTLA-4 could overcome the adaptive immune resistance previously reported with single-agent anti-PD-1 therapy in patients with surgically resectable recurrent glioblastoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Helicobacter pylori triggers gastric mucosal remodeling toward a fetal-like transcriptional program via stromal IL-1β signaling
item.description: During tissue homeostasis, gastric epithelial maintenance is governed by Wnt and BMP signaling, whereas injury induces a YAP-driven fetal-like regenerative program. Here, Beccaceci et al. show that H. pylori infection reprograms the gastric mucosa toward a fetal-like state through BMP deficiency and IL-1β-dependent immune-stromal-epithelial crosstalk.

item.title: Nature Communications: System-wide investments generate health and enhance HIV, TB and malaria control in Malawi
item.description: A modelling study of Malawi’s health system shows that combining health system strengthening with disease-targeted programmes delivers twice the return on investment and three times the health impact of disease-focused investment alone.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cadonilimab plus lenvatinib in advanced endometrial cancer: the multicenter single-arm phase II CLEAR-EC trial
item.description: Immune checkpoint blockade has emerged as a therapeutic option for patients with endometrial cancer. Here the authors report the results of a phase II trial of cadonilimab (a bispecific antibody targeting PD-1 and CTLA-4) combined with lenvatinib in advanced endometrial cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phylogenetic analysis of the 2025 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
item.description: The study reports the emergence of a new Ebola variant in a remote area of Kasai Province, DR Congo. The findings highlight the need for rapid detection and sequencing to better identify variants and quickly respond to outbreaks.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiple local PfDHFR I164L haplotype expansions drive Plasmodium falciparum antifolate resistance in Uganda
item.description: PfDHFR haplotypes involving I164L are known to strongly influence antifolate resistance in Plasmodium falciparum. In this study, Asua and colleagues examine the frequency of antifolate-resistance conferring mutations in over 4,700 parasite samples collected in Uganda over a 6-year period. They report that markers conferring antifolate resistance during this time, which may impact chemotherapeutic strategies that are reliant on sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP).

item.title: Nature Communications: First-line tislelizumab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy in unresectable advanced/metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: minimum 3-year survival follow-up of a randomized phase 3 trial (RATIONALE-306)
item.description: The RATIONALE-306 trial demonstrated improved overall survival in participants with advanced/metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma treated with tislelizumab plus chemotherapy comparing with those who received placebo plus chemotherapy. Here they report its exploratory long-term efficacy/safety/quality of life analysis after 36.0 months follow-up.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extracellular vesicle proteins monitor and interfere with CLDN18.2-targeted CAR-T cell and antibody therapies against gastrointestinal cancers
item.description: CLDN18.2-targeted CART and antibody therapies are promising for gastrointestinal cancers, but predictive biomarkers and strategies to enhance efficacy are needed. Here, these authors investigate how extracellular vesicle (EV)- derived proteins influence therapeutic response to CLDN18.2-based CAR-T and targeted therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microbial-derived tryptophan metabolites in the infant gut associate with increased risk of asthma following cesarean section
item.description: Here, in the Canadian birth cohort (CHILD), the authors associate 1-year C-section-microbiome with higher asthma risk at age 5, as previously reported in the Danish birth cohort (COPSAC2010), and identify microbial-derived tryptophan metabolites at 1 year of age to mediate the association between C-section and asthma risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: A spatial and temporal transcriptomic atlas of mouse intestinal regeneration in the jejunum
item.description: The intestinal epithelium efficiently regenerates after injury, yet the dynamics underlying this process are not fully understood. Here, the authors use spatial transcriptomics to map the mouse intestine over time after radiation injury, revealing shifts in villus zonation, spatially restricted interferon signaling, altered stem cell populations and a surge in gene transcription that may help fuel recovery.

item.title: Nature Communications: The urinary pathobiont Actinobaculum massiliense can generate androgens via the dirAB pathway
item.description: Urinary bacteria linked to prostate cancer are often overlooked. Here, the authors developed a high-throughput assay to identify androgen-producing urinary microbes, isolated key bacterial strains, and discovered genes and enzymes that enable steroid conversion, revealing mechanisms by which urinary bacteria may influence host hormone biology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Motifs of brain cortical folding from birth to adulthood
item.description: Guo and colleagues parse cortical folding variability into a family of distinct anatomical motifs that generalise across adults and neonates. These motifs shed light on structural asymmetry, heritability, and folding-function links.

item.title: Nature Communications: Functional annotation of insulin-responsive genes in human adipocytes reveals PLCXD1 as a lipid storage regulator
item.description: Frendo-Cumbo et al. combine transcriptomics with functional screening in adipocytes to identify PLCXD1 as an insulin-regulated gene. This atypical phospholipase is localized to early endosomes and promotes lipid storage in human fat cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: A fully integrated sample-to-answer diagnostic platform enables rapid quantification of post-transplant infection at the point-of-care
item.description: Opportunistic infections are among the leading causes of graft loss for organ transplant recipients. Here authors introduce a protein-free CRISPR-like assay platform called MONITOR, which, when combined with pre-amplification, achieves single-molecule sensitivity, enabling sample-in-answer-out quantification of post-transplant infections in resource-limited settings.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gene regulatory network analysis identifies auranofin as an anti-atherosclerotic drug
item.description: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are powerful platforms to unravel the genetic complexity of coronary artery disease (CAD). Here, the authors show that a GRN-based drug repurposing coupled with pre-clinical and clinical validation uncovers auranofin as a new potential CAD therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: RAGE mediates LPS-induced inflammatory pain in human skin – a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled full crossover study
item.description: Bacterial lipopolysaccharide induces inflammation. Inflammatory pain is a major clinical challenge lacking suitable and viable human pain models. Here the authors present a double-blind, randomised, placebo controlled full crossover clinical trial examining the pain response to LPS challenge in human skin and suggest a role for RAGE in the LPS-induced inflammatory pain response.

item.title: Nature Communications: Trifluoroacetate mediated reduction of atherosclerosis in mice
item.description: Trifluoroacetate (TFA), long assumed to be an inert peptide counterion, is a bioactive modulator of PPARα signaling that induces peroxisome proliferation, alters lipid metabolism, and attenuates atherosclerosis in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sex- and fiber type-specific remodeling of the muscle proteome implicates CSRP3 in resistance training-induced hypertrophy
item.description: Here, the authors show that changes in the muscle fiber proteome following 8 weeks of resistance training are both sex- and fiber type-specific. This includes greater upregulation of CSRP3 in type II than type I fibers, which in mice was shown to be involved in muscle growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Subtyping metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease using electronic health record-linked genomic cohorts reveals diverse etiologies and progression
item.description: From multi-year Mayo Clinic records on liver disease, researchers identified five distinct patient patterns. The method for generating liver disease subtypes is robust, producing transferable subtypes across diverse patient cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Biomechanical energy harvesting to improve post-stroke mobility
item.description: Foot drop after stroke reduces toe clearance and walking safety. Here, Pan et al . report a gait-timing-adaptive, self-powered neuroprosthesis that harvests gait energy to augment ankle dorsiflexion, improving outdoor walking distance and speed, and reducing gait variability in stroke survivors.

item.title: Nature Communications: Efficacy of everolimus and letrozole with or without ribociclib in recurrent endometrial cancer: a phase 2 randomized clinical trial
item.description: Therapeutic options for recurrent endometrial cancer (rEC) are limited. Here, the authors present a randomized phase 2 clinical trial comparing the combination of mTOR and aromatase inhibitors (everolimus and letrozole) with or without the CDK4/6 inhibitor, ribociclib, in patients with rEC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global incidence of esophageal cancer by histological and anatomical subtypes
item.description: There is a need for more insights into subtype differences, temporal trends and related risk factors of oesophageal cancer. Here, the authors find that the incidence, risk factors, and trends of oesophageal cancer vary significantly by histological and anatomical subtypes in different populations globally.

item.title: Nature Communications: The Fanconi anemia pathway restrains MLL-rearranged leukemogenesis through suppressing non-homologous end joining-mediated genomic instability
item.description: Mutations in the Fanconi anemia (FA) DNA repair genes predispose to leukemia and bone marrow failure. Here, the authors discover that the FA pathway controls MLL-rearranged leukemia progression via blocking nonhomologous end joining-mediated genomic instability.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cell-type specific analyses in blood and gut identify cis-eQTL matching 140 IBD risk loci and entrectinib as repurposing candidate
item.description: Inflammatory bowel disease risk variants can identify genes and pathways involved in disease mechanisms. Here, the authors integrate blood and intestinal eQTL maps with patient gene expression data to prioritise candidate drug targets and identify entrectinib as a potential repurposing candidate.

item.title: Nature Communications: FBXW7 mitigates hepatic fibrosis by degrading NOTCH1 to transcriptionally silence SEMA3G in liver sinusoidal endothelial cells
item.description: The authors reported a randomized trial showing that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation reduces postoperative liver injury in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vivo effect of anti-PD-1 on HIV-specific CD8+T-cells in men with HIV
item.description: In people living with HIV, long term viral infection, even in the face of successful therapeutic control of viral load, can result in increased numbers of exhausted CD8 + T cells. Here the authors assess the in vivo effect of anti-PD-1 antibody therapy on the HIV specific CD8 + T cell response in men with HIV.

item.title: Nature Communications: Identifying a broad-spectrum influenza inhibitor that blocks multiple functions of viral NS1 protein
item.description: This study identifies a broad-spectrum IAV inhibitor that blocks multiple functions of NS1 protein. The critical sites on NS1 targeted by the inhibitor are validated in vitro and in vivo, supporting the possibility for anti-IAV therapy targeting NS1.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multidisciplinary intervention in frail elderly patients with cardiovascular diseases: a multicentre, single-blinded, randomised controlled trial
item.description: A hospital-initiated multidisciplinary program was associated with improved frailty and physical function and lower readmission risk in frail elderly patients with cardiovascular diseases, although larger studies are needed to confirm these.

item.title: Nature Communications: Perirenal fat β₃-adrenergic signaling alleviates renal fibrosis via regulating Bcat2/BCAA-TNFα pathway in diabetic kidney disease
item.description: The authors identify perirenal fat ADRB3 signaling as a regulator of diabetic kidney fibrosis through a Bcat2/BCAA-TNFα pathway, suggesting adipose-kidney crosstalk as a potential therapeutic target.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clinical attribute-based risk matrix for prognostication in immunotherapy-treated non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: Current biomarkers used to guide immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) do not adequately stratify patients for prognosis. Here, the authors show that CLARITY-ICI Matrix, a clinically deployable, missing-data-tolerant framework, enables population-aware stratification of survival risk in immunotherapy-treated NSCLC using routinely available clinical attributes and complements biomarkers.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neoadjuvant anti-HER2 antibody-drug conjugate SHR-A1811 in Hormone Receptor-positive, HER2-low Breast Cancer: A Phase 2 Clinical Trial (HELEN-015)
item.description: Anti-HER2 antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have been approved for patients with Hormone Receptor positive (HR + ), HER2-low metastatic breast cancer. Here, the authors present a phase II interventional clinical trial evaluating the anti-HER2 ADC SHR-A1811 as neoadjuvant monotherapy in patients with HR + HER2-low breast cancer (HELEN-015).

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-cell profiling identifies obesity-disrupted brain glucose sensing
item.description: How obesity disrupts central glucose sensing remains poorly understood. Here, the authors use single-cell transcriptomics to identify hypothalamic and hindbrain neurons that respond to elevated blood glucose and show these responses are impaired in obesity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gut microbiota-activated PLCγ2 monocytes drive atrial fibrillation
item.description: Atrial fibrillation involves systemic inflammatory activation that remodel the atrial endocardium. Here, the authors show that gut microbiota activate PLCy2 positive monocytes, promoting endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and atrial fibrillation through a microbiota–monocyte–endocardial axis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hybrid exosomal nanomotors convert pathological ROS into transport-driving cues to enhance cartilage accumulation in osteoarthritis
item.description: Osteoarthritis therapies are limited by poor drug transport within dense cartilage. Here, authors develop hybrid exosomal nanomotors that convert pathological ROS into transport-driving cues, enhancing transport within cartilage and slowing osteoarthritis progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Brain-cognition relationships and treatment outcome in treatment-resistant late-life depression
item.description: Late-life depression is hard to treat and presents a risk for dementia. Here, the authors identify neural correlates of cognitive function in late-life depression, and pinpoint clinical symptoms, gray matter loss and worse cognition as robust baseline markers of non-remission to antidepressants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distinct multi-omics signatures of clinical subgroups of type 2 diabetes define heterogeneous responses to an insulin sensitizer
item.description: The authors identified molecular signatures for type 2 diabetes subgroups in Chinese patients using multi-omics data. These signatures enhance drug response predictions, supporting personalized diabetes management.

item.title: Nature Communications: Associations between diet quality, epigenetic aging and epigenome in two population-based cohorts
item.description: The specific healthy diet may matter less than eating healthily overall. In two German cohorts, several healthy diets were each linked to slower biological aging, with distinct DNA methylation patterns that converged on shared pathways.

item.title: Nature Communications: DNA methylation profiling identifies long-range epigenetic silencing of clustered protocadherins as a key determinant of meningioma progression
item.description: The molecular drivers of meningioma progression remain poorly understood. Here, the authors profile DNA methylation in cross-sectional and longitudinal meningioma cohorts and identify molecular features of benign and aggressive disease and microevolutionary adaptation during progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: GRAF1-dependent endocytotic processes and the Golgi apparatus contribute to previously unrecognized intermediate stages of early ciliogenesis
item.description: A three-dimensional ultrastructural analysis reveals previously unrecognized intermediate stages in the formation of primary cilia. It is demonstrated that both the endocytotic protein GRAF1 and the Golgi apparatus contribute to the intracellular pathway of ciliogenesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Wireless IoT-enabled microneedle electroceutical for personalized and connected pain management
item.description: Skin-attached electrotherapeutic devices suffer from unstable skin-electrode interface. Here, the authors present a thermoresponsive conductive adhesive microneedle electroceutical providing stable, safe stimulation and IoT-based personalized pain therapy with healthcare-provider oversight.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD97/ ADGRE5 attenuates the induction of adaptive type 2 immune responses in allergic asthma
item.description: Allergic asthma involves different lung cells and mediators. Here, the authors examine the function of CD97/ ADGRE5 and show that its absence increases the severity of allergic lung inflammation in mice. Allergen-pulsed Cd97 -/- DCs are more activated and promote stronger type 2 immune responses than WT DCs and, in humans, lung DCs from allergen-exposed asthmatics express less CD97 than allergic non-asthmatics.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD38-activated macrophages drive age-related placental senescence by depleting NAD + in decidual stromal cells
item.description: The authors show that CD38-activated macrophages deplete NAD+ in decidual stromal cells, driving placental senescence and fetal growth restriction during aging. NAD+ restoration in animal models improves pregnancy outcomes and offspring health.

item.title: Nature Communications: Disitamab vedotin for HER2-positive breast cancer with liver metastases: phase 3 results from the RC48-C006 phase 2/3 trial
item.description: Patients with HER2-positive breast cancer with liver metastases (BCLM) have poor prognosis. Here, the authors report phase 3 results from the phase 2/3 RC48-C006 clinical trial comparing disitamab vedotin (HER2 targeted antibody drug conjugate) against lapatinib plus capecitabine in patients with HER2-postivie breast cancer with liver metastases previously treated with trastuzumab and taxanes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Risk factors for major depressive disorder among adults recruited from hospital settings in Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and South Africa
item.description: Across Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and South Africa, a harmonized study identified factors associated with major depression and found country differences explained 24% of variation, indicating regional strategies should be adapted to national contexts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial analysis reveals cellular microenvironments and mechanisms of inflammation and injury in acute interstitial nephritis
item.description: Spatial analysis of human kidney biopsies reveals that acute interstitial nephritis differs from nonimmune kidney injury, identifying complement-producing injured tubules, T cell signaling and NAMPT as markers of sustained inflammatory niches.

item.title: Nature Communications: An FGF21-IGFBP1 tumor-liver relay drives musculoskeletal defects in colorectal cancer cachexia
item.description: Colorectal cancer often causes cachexia, a wasting syndrome that weakens muscles and bones. Here, the authors show that a tumor-liver signaling relay driven by FGF21 and IGFBP1 promotes this decline, identifying a potential target to preserve musculoskeletal health.

item.title: Nature Communications: Integration of GWAS and single-cell analysis for psoriasis identifies disease-associated cell subtypes and therapeutic targets
item.description: Integrating genetic data and skin single-cell data highlights psoriasis-associated cell types and cell type-specific functional mechanisms. These findings offer perspectives for identifying therapeutic targets for psoriasis at the cellular level.

item.title: Nature Communications: An AI-powered self-driving microscope for low-cost acute leukemia detection
item.description: Current AI systems for leukemia detection typically rely on costly whole-slide scanners, limiting accessibility in low-resource settings. Here, the authors present ALLocate, a low-cost, AI-driven microscope plugin that enables self-driving microscopy for accurate and affordable leukemia detection without whole-slide scanners.

item.title: Nature Communications: The cortical microenvironment drives early immune organization and controls early osteoclastogenesis in bone healing
item.description: Here they identify a specialized cortical niche that coordinates immune and stromal cells to drive early osteoclast formation during fracture healing and show that aging primarily impairs this supportive microenvironment rather than the cells themselves.

item.title: Nature Communications: A machine-assisted framework for systematic error analysis in clinical concept extraction
item.description: MedError, a machine-assisted human-in-the-loop framework, improves the standardization, validity, and efficiency of clinical NLP error analysis, supporting more transparent and trustworthy model deployment.
